test.name: Execute a planned 1850 census search and log the result
test.description: Execute plan item pli_001 (1850 census for Patrick Flynn in Schuylkill County, FamilySearch). After record_search (with projectPath) stages the results, passing subjectId ranks them against subject I1 inline (attachments folded in). The fixture returns the expected matching household as a strong, unattached top match. Tests whether the skill (a) constructs the search parameters from the plan item, (b) writes a proper log entry, and (c) triages the ranked results without silently dropping near-matches.

input.user_message: Execute a fresh 1850 census search for Patrick Flynn in Schuylkill County for plan item pli_001. Prior log entries on this plan item used different query parameters and were inconclusive — log this new search regardless.

judge_context: record_search ranks host-side when it is called with projectPath AND subjectId, returning the ranking inline as `ranked` (match score + attachment flag for every candidate). The skill should pass subjectId and triage from `ranked` — NOT per-result same_person, NOT a separate source_attachments call, and NOT a separate rank_search_matches call (the search folds all three in).
The log entry's `query` should reflect the actual search parameters used (name, place, year/collection) and `results_examined` should match the count returned by the record_search fixture

Must NOT set pli_001 status to 'completed' — the plan item status should remain 'in_progress' after the search; 'completed' is only set once the results have been extracted and analyzed by record-extraction downstream

Using the ranked matches as a review surface, the skill should triage the top match (a strong, unattached census hit — surfaced as new evidence to prioritize for extraction) rather than silently filtering it, and categorize any near-matches in `notes` instead of dropping them

Tool Arguments: score 3 if record_search was called with projectPath AND subjectId (subjectId is what triggers host-side ranking) plus appropriate search parameters. A validate_research_schema call with a project path after writing is acceptable and expected — do not penalize it. Only score 2 if record_search had clearly wrong arguments, or omitted subjectId when the research subject is known. Do NOT expect a separate rank_search_matches call — ranking is part of record_search now.

IMPORTANT — How file writes work: `research_log_append` writes the log entry AND the results/ sidecar host-side from the staged handle; the skill does not hand-write either. Sidecars are newly created files, so they never appear in the file-change diff — their absence from it is not evidence of anything.
